claims.statement: Behavioral evals under evals/ score non-deterministic skill judgment against labeled ground truth, and their LLM runs are triggered manually rather than in CI while scoring is deterministic and scripted.

The review-chain benchmark measures only whether /correctness-review and /intent-review catch the planted defect classes in its fixtures; its numbers are not evidence about the full workflow chain or real-world catch rate (not_observed != absent).

Each review-chain fixture contains intent.md, a diff.patch with exactly one planted defect, truth.md, and a machine-readable truth.json naming the expected oracle, core and correctness_clean flags, a planted pattern, and false-positive patterns.
run_review_chain_eval.py sends a fixed two-oracle prompt with intent.md and diff.patch inlined to claude -p with no tools from an empty temporary directory, so the reviewer never sees the answer key.

score_review_chain_eval.py reads findings from the last fenced json block that parses as a JSON array and marks a reply unparseable, rather than zero findings, when it mentions a json fence but no block parses as an array.

The review-chain scorer classifies class-unknown findings as other, then planted (file plus match_any plus and_any match), then listed false positives, and treats any correctness finding on a correctness_clean fixture as a false positive; a fixture is caught when any finding is planted, with oracle_match recording whether it came from the expected oracle.

Errored, unparseable, and not-run review-chain fixtures are excluded from the totals instead of scored as misses, token totals include errored cases, and --score exits 1 when no fixture could be scored.

Review-chain confidence values must be plain decimals; non-numeric or non-finite values are warned about and treated as 0, numeric values are clamped to 0-100, and false positives at or above --threshold (default 75) are counted separately.

run_review_prompt_eval.py A/B-tests the real reviewer prompts of two git revisions under identical fixed conditions (safe mode, Read-only tool, clean temp directory without truth files, per-call and total budget caps), never reruns a recorded call, publishes records atomically, and is manual and not part of CI.

The test-runner eval runs the agent body as a system prompt via claude -p with only Bash, Read, Glob and Grep tools, project-only settings and strict MCP config, and records reports, Bash commands, usage, and a before/after hash of every repo file.

A test-runner eval case passes only if the verdict, failing-test recall, absence of false failures, Failed+Errors count, and required mentions all match, the agent ran pytest itself, and no repo file changed; diagnosis is scored separately.

Hard-gate respect is the non-negotiable intake metric: a fixture whose truth declares a hard gate must be classified high-risk, and score_intake_eval.py --strict exits 1 when any hard-gate fixture is downgraded.

run_intake_eval.py runs each fixture in a scratch git worktree at the eval.json pinned from commit, deletes evals/ from it, deploys the branch harness config into it, and refuses to pass --bare to the client.
run_intake_eval.py copies the scorer and fixtures out of the repo before any fixture runs and scores with that copy, so agent edits to the in-tree scorer or answer keys cannot change the score.

An intake fixture is marked stray when any file outside its may_change globs (fnmatch) changes or any repo ref is created, deleted or moved; the runner exits 1 when any fixture is not ok or the scorer fails, and refuses an existing output directory.
The intake runner's blinding covers writes only: the agent can still read truth.md in the main checkout or git history by absolute path.
score_intake_eval.py does not assert lane for expected_lane any, and matches expected flags by normalized alphanumeric substring so separator and parenthetical variations still match.

Context-boundary probes are a manual protocol with no automated runner that test instruction delivery per context with a positive marker (auto-correct-scope heading after explicit Read) and a negative control (wave-parallelism rule referenced but not read).

In context-boundary probes, main-session results do not transfer to child contexts, the implementer, reviewer and scorer contexts are load-bearing so an unconfirmed verdict there blocks or lowers confidence, and results are pinned to claude --version and must be re-probed after upgrades.

score_skill_eval.py never calls a model; --compare fails on environment mismatch, pass-to-missed or false-positive regressions, new false positives, safety-critical misses, and suite pass-count drops, while a pass-to-blocked change is reported as unmeasured coverage rather than a regression.

score_skill_eval.py --validate-corpus requires every skill registered in harness-manifest.json to have activation cases with at least 8 should-trigger and 8 near-miss cases each including a holdout, behavior cases of golden, boundary and handoff kinds, and the five named end-to-end canaries.
Skill-eval result records must have first_run true and a non-empty observation, and results must state model, client_version and reasoning.

CI's run-tests.sh validates review-chain answer keys with score_review_chain_eval.py --check-truth, which checks truth.json schema, required fixture files, and that planted.file appears in diff.patch.

CI's pytest step collects every test_*.py under scripts, runtime and skills, which covers the eval runners and scorers with stub clients, and deliberately excludes evals/ because fixture repos contain intentionally failing tests.
run-tests.sh does not run score_skill_eval.py, so a missing prompt-refactor corpus entry for a newly registered skill is not caught by CI.
A CI unit test re-runs each test-runner fixture's pytest suite and checks its truth.json against the real outcome so answer keys cannot drift from the fixture code.

Eval honesty rules require that the first scored run is the record, fixtures are not re-run until they pass, and answer-key revisions are logged with prior results marked not comparable on the revised fixture.

The review-chain corpus is meant to grow from real escapes: fixed rows in docs/review-escapes.md should map to a regression fixture, test, or documented won't-fix, and escape-seeded fixtures should point back to their ledger row.

A reviewer prompt change that alters what a reviewer checks is proven by two runs of the real reviewer agent with the real prompt: a canary that acts as the gate, passing only when every planted defect gets the expected severity and no clean control gets a finding, and a historical replay of a previously approved case that is recorded as evidence and is not a gate.

Canary fixtures live under specs/<slug>/canary/ with the record in specs/<slug>/canary.md, are built with the same task_brief.py and review_package.py scripts that a real dispatch uses, and a plan can gate on the line `Canary result: pass` via grep.

The gh-312 canary planted an off-seam test and a test whose expected value was computed by the code under test next to two clean controls; the task-reviewer flagged both planted tests as Important, flagged neither control, surfaced a hidden tab-splitting bug, and the record states Canary result: pass.

The gh-175 Task 2.1 replay with the seam check returned needs_fixes where the original per-task review approved, matching later gh-175 correctness findings [A/B] and [C] (synthetic-only fixtures, per-entry SHA association) but not the other nine code defects; it ran against today's tree, which holds more real runs than existed at the time.

Blind skill-eval runs are dispatched by the orchestrator as one subagent per fixture that never sees truth.md; a standalone or CI runner requiring ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is deliberately not built because an LLM in CI is costly and flaky.

The blind-run playbook requires multiple runs because one run hides non-determinism (four intake runs kept hard-gate respect at 3/3 while one lane-boundary fixture flipped tiny/normal), and requires marking decisions the fixture already states as settled-by-fixture before the first run so only open rows are scored.

skills/diagnosing-bugs/tests/routing-cases.md is a manual routing canary table run by a human or a meta-eval session, not per-commit CI; because the skill sets disable-model-invocation: true, feature-intake routes bug fixes by reading the SKILL.md, so a Skill call in the chaining case means the route failed.

The diagnosing-bugs routing canaries cover an over-firing case (a quick question starts no diagnosis), the feature-intake chaining case, direct /diagnosing-bugs invocation, and design decision D4 that a tiny-lane bug fix still runs all six phases with no cause-known shortcut.
